kicker: Management changes · the first call after a CEO, CFO or MD change
title: New boss, new tone: the first call after a change
dek: NIIT's call score fell from 63 to 41 on its first call under a new CEO, who cut the FY27 revenue view to flat; Apollo Tyres and SKF India (Industrial) dropped to the 40 cap, while South Indian Bank rose from 58 to 61.

stats.note: Q2 revenue fell 6.4% after a double-digit Q2 guide; new CEO's review takes 60–90 days.

read: The first call under new leadership is often where guidance gets reset; NIIT's 60–90 day review makes its Q3 call the next marker.
sources: Vantage analysis of management-change filings on BSE and Q4 FY26–Q2 FY27 earnings calls; Q2 FY27 results filed on BSE
notes: Vantage call score (0–100) on the last call before a CEO, CFO or MD change was filed vs the first call after it. A score of 40 is the cap applied when a call drops guidance without explanation or carries a serious red flag: Apollo Tyres dropped its full-year Europe EBITDA guide on its Q2 call. NIIT named Anish Sarkar CEO on 14 Oct 2026; on the 3 Nov call the company said: “we are, at this point of time, looking at the rest of the year and going by the experience of this quarter, assuming that the revenue is likely to be broadly flat.” Apollo Tyres' CFO resigned on 6 Oct and a new CFO was named on 4 Nov (call 6 Nov), in a quarter when raw-material costs rose about 25%. SKF India (Industrial) announced its MD handover on 11 Aug (effective 1 Sep), before its Q1 FY27 call; its score recovered to 55 on the Q2 call. South Indian Bank's new MD & CEO took over on 1 Oct; Info Edge announced its CEO exit on 28 Oct, two days before the call. Scores also reflect results, so a shift cannot be put down to the change alone.
